answer: Deposits are visible in willow, and velvet reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 15% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 143 aliases, and each one needs its own funded copper account. That bill is paid per identity, so 61 aliases cost 195 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
